ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data): {"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABbHHcfQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhEsQkI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 118, "title": "Make the emulator the visual focus and demote bundled game branding", "body": "## Problem The browser UI now has a working one-tap bundled demo and complete responsive mobile controls (completed in [Issue #116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116) / [PR #117](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/117)). However, the page's visual hierarchy still makes **潮鳴りの密室 / Shionari no Misshitsu** look like the main product rather than a demo of **snes-rust**, a general-purpose SNES emulator. In the current [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), the sidebar has `BUNDLED ADVENTURE`, a prominent `

潮鳴りの密室

` and a separate romanized subtitle. In [`web/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), that title uses 26px while the actual `snes-rust` heading is 21px. The demo/game identity has stronger typographic emphasis than the emulator brand. The result can be mistaken for the game's promotional website and is awkward when users load unrelated cartridges. The maintainer's direction: **The product is the emulator. The bundled game is just one immediately playable example. Prioritize the generic screen/player and the two entry actions, rather than a game-specific hero section.** ## Expected outcome The first visual read of the browser page is **“snes-rust — a SNES emulator”**, followed by its large generic game screen/player and straightforward actions. The current bundled game remains easy to try in **one action** but its title is presented only as compact, subordinate metadata (such as a small caption under “Try demo”), not as a large heading or promotional masthead. The UI should feel equally natural when a user plays the bundled demo **or imports any supported local SNES ROM**. Keep the clean, light, minimal visual style and the existing mobile experience. This is a focused hierarchy/copy/layout refinement, not a broad redesign or an emulator behavior change. ## Context and proposed UI hierarchy On desktop / large viewports: 1. **Brand / app identity:** clear, succinct `snes-rust` heading in the header. Optionally a subtle “SNES emulator” descriptor; do not add long product pitches. 2. **Main player:** large, visually dominant generic emulated screen. Before a ROM is loaded, use the neutral existing placeholder, not a fictional or game-specific hero image. Once loaded, show actual emulated pixels without promotional overlays. 3. **Game entry actions:** concise **“Try demo / デモで試す”** action with the game's name as *small secondary text*, alongside a clear **“Open ROM / ROMを開く”** action for the user's own cartridges. One-tap demo launch remains. Neither action needs a giant game title above it. 4. **Playback tools:** compact Play/Pause, Reset, Sound, Fullscreen and status/error indicators, with Help/Controls and About/Legal in their existing disclosures. The exact arrangement may be tuned for sensible responsive behavior, but **do not** turn the screen into a card for a specific game or present Shionari artwork/title as the app's brand. Avoid gratuitous iconography and decorations; show purpose through spacing, grouping and sizing. ### Functional and responsive constraints - Preserve all working [Issue #116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116) behavior: one-tap demo download/validation/autoplay and user-gesture audio handling; local ROM picker; playback lifecycle; SRAM key isolation and failed-save/restore safety; accessibility/error states; native gamepad/keyboard and multitouch virtual controller. - On **desktop**, keep the screen the dominant area with a lightweight set of nearby actions. Make the emulator name more recognizable than any game title. The demo name may appear inside its option/caption and the current game identity can be indicated unobtrusively when loaded. - On **portrait mobile**, minimize vertical space spent on game-specific title text so the screen and all 12 SNES controls remain usable. The emulator label, Try demo, Open ROM, and essential playback controls stay recognizable. - On **short-height landscape mobile**, keep the existing center-screen / left-D-pad / right-face-buttons layout, with L/R and Start/Select accessible. Do not reintroduce a large title area, clipped controls, unnecessary scrolling or video occlusion. - Preserve keyboard focus labels, error and audio feedback, needed storage/privacy guidance and legally required ROM credits. The full Shionari provenance/license notice remains accessible under About/Legal; simplifying the first view must not hide essential recovery errors. - Prefer changes within `web/index.html`, `web/style.css` and minimal associated JS/tests. Do not add a framework, modify `demos/shionari.sfc`, introduce another ROM, or replace the preview with generated game art. ## Pre-merge acceptance - [ ] The desktop page clearly brands **snes-rust** as the emulator. The bundled game does **not** have a larger or more dominant heading than the application name; remove the `BUNDLED ADVENTURE` promotional hierarchy and redundant large Japanese/romanized title block, replacing it with small contextual demo metadata where useful. - [ ] The primary game screen remains visually dominant on desktop; **Try demo** and **Open ROM** are readily discoverable and visually grouped as alternative ways to use the emulator. Neither requires reading long prose. - [ ] In a clean browser session, one deliberate activation of Try demo still fetches the pinned bundled ROM, starts genuine Wasm emulation and updates frames without a second Play action. Loading a local ROM uses the same secure cartridge/save pipeline and naturally updates any current-game label without preserving Shionari as the apparent product identity. - [ ] Desktop, narrow portrait and short landscape screenshots **of the actual implementation** demonstrate the intended hierarchy and that the screen, Play/Pause, and all 12 accessible touch controls remain visible/usable. Verify safe-area handling, resizing, fullscreen and no horizontal overflow at the viewports exercised in #116. - [ ] Automated browser assertions check meaningful user-facing hierarchy or visibility (app title, subdued demo label, grouped demo/local entry actions), alongside existing real DOM/controller/gameplay behavior. Do not rely only on fragile CSS snapshots. Update only selectors affected by the new markup without weakening tests. - [ ] Preserve pause/reset/audio/gesture behavior, gamepad and keyboard input, touch multi-press/diagonals/cancellation, SRAM persistence/recovery, legal disclosure, Pages CSP and `/snes-rust/` asset URLs. No user-supplied ROM/SRAM uploads. - [ ] Run the relevant production site build and full mandatory Chromium/Playwright suite including Pages smoke, plus the repository's CI checks appropriate to the diff. Report actual results and unchanged source-built game and hardware regressions accurately; do not claim checks that were not run. - [ ] Include concise before/after design rationale and actual desktop/portrait/landscape screenshots in the PR or validation note. Preserve the three documented [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): Keep it simple, Show don't tell, and Intuitive and predictable. ## Optional validation Quick usability feedback from a new visitor who has never seen Shionari, plus physical mobile browser review. No design approval or physical device is mandatory when the stated browser checks pass. ## Required post-merge verification The PR author/merger should inspect the resulting `main` Pages workflow and, after deployment, visually confirm the actual public page retains the new emulator-first hierarchy on desktop and mobile with functioning demo/local-ROM choices. This is **not a pre-merge acceptance condition**. If publication fails, open a separate `task` Issue with the failing run, URLs and evidence. No background monitoring is implied. ## Related work - [Issue #116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116) / [PR #117](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/117): current responsive/touch UI baseline. - [Issue #110](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/110): bundled demo integration and legal notice.
